theReleaseRuleAndWhyThePrefixIdentifiesT.rule: A value cell on one of this job's three corpus rails is released when its own `source` starts with `@empressaio/setback-corpus@` and the version after that prefix is strictly OLDER than the pinned CORPUS_VERSION, compared component-wise as int[] (so 1.10.0 is newer than 1.4.0). It is then re-resolved under the pin and either re-stamped, written with the pin's different value (named old-beside-new), or given the writer's current disposition for that rail -- per rail, never half a parcel.
theReleaseRuleAndWhyThePrefixIdentifiesT.whyThePrefixIsUniqueToThisJobOnTheseRail: CORPUS_SOURCE_PREFIX is composed from CORPUS_PACKAGE and CORPUS_VERSION in one place and the literal prefix is typed in no expression anywhere in src/; exactly two files in src/ compose a corpus source at all (this job and parcel-setback-cells.mjs); and their rail sets are DISJOINT. All four facts are asserted by the identity tests rather than commented, so a future writer on an envelope rail fails the suite before it can be silently absorbed by the release. Measured on the store: the other-producer arm is EMPTY in the six counties.
theReleaseRuleAndWhyThePrefixIdentifiesT.whereItLives: isStaleCorpusValueCell / corpusVersionFromSource / compareCorpusVersions / corpusSourceOrder / hasStaleCorpusEffect (imported from parcel-setback-cells.mjs) and staleCorpusValueGateSql, interpolated into UPDATE_ENVELOPE_CELLS_SQL through envelopeCellGateSql so the statement carries the shared expression rather than a copy; envelopeCellMayBeMoved mirrors the whole WHERE for the pure-predicate direction.

ONE helper did move to shared ground -- corpusTableDateFields in src/lib/setback-writer/setback-table-router.mjs, now the single producer of the sourceDate/dateBasis vocabulary for BOTH corpus writers.

The chunk rows name each cell's OLD cited version, so which cells moved and from what is recoverable; the values themselves cannot need restoring (a re-stamp moves none), and the date fields the re-stamp adds (sourceDate/dateBasis) are an addition, so a reversal is a field-level edit to up to 709,945 rows, not a job. threeQuestionGate.whatExecutesTheRelease: The job's own write gate, at the moment each page's UPDATE is issued. processCityPage reads the page's parcels and their three rails' current states once, planStaleCorpusRelease decides per RAIL from what each cell itself says (its own source, its own recorded jurisdictionKey/districtCode/inputs), the released cells join the same cellBatch as every other write in the job, and envelopeCellGateSql interpolates P-363's staleCorpusValueGateSql as the fourth alternative of the statement's WHERE -- so the release is admitted by the same statement that admits a first write, and the pure predicate is pinned to that statement in both directions. No flag, no second code path, no manual step.
threeQuestionGate.whatTriggersIt: Any run of the job after a corpus pin move -- the scheduled Cloud Run job factory-parcel-envelope-cells or the factory CLI, for any in-scope county. There is no switch to turn on and nothing to remember: the trigger is the pin (@empressaio/setback-corpus's CORPUS_VERSION) being newer than the version a cell cites. This lane's own dry runs were the trigger WITHOUT the write: apply=false and no run id, which is precisely why the release's record path refuses rather than silently skipping.
threeQuestionGate.whatFailsWhenAStaleCorpusValueSurvives: In the order a reader hits them: (1) the CITATION is false -- the cell tells a reader it came from the corpus at 1.1.0 while the image pins 1.4.0, which is the defect P-363 fixed for setbacks; (2) the ledger's provenance is wrong at the version level, on rails that a district + setback table is supposed to answer for; (3) the failure is INVISIBLE to CI -- both the falsifier suite and the live gate test PASS while all 709,945 cells remain stale, because staleness is a data state, not a code state; that is exactly why this row's instruments are the store census and the per-county dry run rather than the suite; (4) no record exists, so a stale population has no trail naming which cells need it -- the run_events chunk rows are the only artifact that names the move, and they are written only when the move happens.
threeQuestionGate.whatBypassesIt: (a) A HAND UPDATE to parcel_record_cell that never runs this job: no gate, no record -- named, not hidden, and out of this lane's control. (b) A SECOND WRITER on the three envelope rails: today the store shows the other-producer arm EMPTY and the identity tests assert the tree properties that would make a new writer detectable, but the release trusts that prefix, so a writer that reused the envelope rails with a corpus-shaped source would be absorbed silently -- the identity suite is the control that makes it fail loudly instead. (c) A PIN MOVED WITHOUT A RE-RUN: the release is only as current as the last run of the job, and nothing in the row forces a run after a pin move (a schedule does, and that is the operational answer). (d) A PARTIAL APPLY: Williamson 48491's apply belongs to P-350, so the seat can legitimately apply the other five counties and leave 48491 stale for a while -- the record's per-county counts and the releasedVersions list are how that is seen. (e) The FOOTPRINT CARRY: a footprint whose recorded coverage input has not moved is not re-derived, by design, bounded by a falsifier with a paired control.
